title: Nearly half a million Indian workers passed through one Mauritius site
body: From 1834 to 1920, almost half a million indentured labourers arrived at Aapravasi Ghat in Port Louis. Some worked in Mauritius's sugar plantations and others were sent on to destinations including Reunion and the Caribbean.
takeaway: A single immigration depot can help explain why communities with Indian roots formed across distant islands.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Aapravasi Ghat (2006)
visual: worn stone steps rising from the waterfront at an old immigration depot

title: The ILO estimated that more than half of workers were informal
body: The International Labour Organization estimated in 2018 that about 2 billion people worked informally, around 61% of the world's employed population. That includes jobs without some of the arrangements typical of formal employment.
takeaway: A census of registered firms alone can miss a large share of how people make a living.
source: International Labour Organization, Women and Men in the Informal Economy (2018)
visual: a group of informal repair and produce stalls on a village street
